newsitem.title: CHINA: China needs to control rubber imports in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China needs to control rubber imports in 1997.

text.p: China must control rubber imports to prevent a glut on the domestic market this year, the China Chemical Industry News said on Thursday.
China ought to limit average monthly imports to about 30,000 tonnes due to strong levels of imports in 1996 and existing stockpiles of about 20,000 tonnes, the newspaper said.

Rising production capacity and sluggish demand from ailing domestic firms were other factors contributing to the need for import curbs, it said. China imported 160,000 tonnes of natural rubber, including latex, in the first four months, up by 15.5 percent from the same period of 1996, customs figure showed. Imports for April alone were 50,000 tonnes.
Imports of synthetic rubber, including latex, in the first four months were 124,291 tonnes, up by 9.0 percent. Imports for April alone were 34,918 tonnes.
Domestic demand this year was estimated at about 1.68 million tonnes, the newspaper said.
China planned to produce 430,000 tonnes of natural rubber and 620,000 tonnes of synthetic rubber this year, it said.
China produced 47,400 tonnes of synthetic rubber in January, up 1.9 percent from the same period of last year, the newspaper said, attributing the production growth to the addition of new equipment.
Current domestic rubber prices remained at low levels and were unlikely to rebound this year due to sufficient supply, the newspaper said.
Spot domestic prices of some kinds of rubber dropped to 12,200 yuan ($1,469) per tonne from 16,000 yuan January 1996, it said.
